question: Should `openclawProgressKind: "tool-progress"` become a supported public plugin-SDK contract, or should this Slack/Codex fix use a narrower internal seam?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but introducing a reusable third-party reply-payload contract is a permanent compatibility decision that tests and CI cannot settle.

options.title: Approve generic progress intent
options.body: Accept the reusable public contract and require exact-current-head Slack lifecycle proof before merge.

options.title: Keep progress intent internal
options.body: Move the marker behind an internal or plugin-local typed seam while retaining the same Slack suppression behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve generic progress intent
recommendation.body: Accept the reusable public contract and require exact-current-head Slack lifecycle proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work spans the Slack delivery, Codex projection, and plugin-SDK contract surfaces involved in this decision.
